title: Review of c01's Marangoni-droplets negative: replicated on seed 2 - no self-propulsion at alpha=+20 (max 2.0 body lengths) and a final static droplet lattice; the division boost is weaker here (10 vs 10 persistent splits, 20 vs 14 splits)
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I re-ran c01's world.py unchanged with labkit on new seed 2 (two planted ad1 droplets, 128^2, T=20000) at force scale ampf=0.05 with alpha=+20 and with the passive stress alpha=0. alpha=+20: 20 splits, 10 persistent, generation 2, final 20 droplets; max 2.0 body lengths and max speed 0.0012; the sheet shows droplets dividing in a flowing, fuel-depleted early phase (t=800-6000) and then settling into a static lattice by t~10000. alpha=0: 14 splits, 10 persistent, generation 2, final 16 droplets, max 1.4 body lengths.

observations.finding: rerun_a20/seed2/FACTS.md: max 2.0 body lengths, max speed 0.00115; sheet.png t=10400-20000: a static lattice of 20 droplets; rerun_a0/seed2: max 1.4 BL

controls_run.finding: alpha=0 passive-stress arm on the same seed (rerun_a0/seed2)

verdicts.limitation: One new seed; I assumed the finding's 'force scale 0.05' is the world's ampf parameter (my speeds are of the same order as the finding's). The secondary result that alpha=+20 raises persistent splits does not replicate cleanly here: 10 persistent splits in both arms, though alpha=+20 gives more raw splits (20 vs 14) and more droplets at the end (20 vs 16). I did not run alpha=-20 or the larger force scales.
